story: Alaska Data Corporation and InvestNorth, the state's tokenized data center finance launch of November 9th, and the January AIDEA resolution that funded it

repeat_reasons.reason: The first response paraphrased the officer lines rather than quoting them. One targeted repeat captured the exact President and Vice President lines and the exact subsidiary sentence. No other URL was fetched twice.

claims.claim: Gov. Mike Dunleavy announced Alaska Data Corporation and InvestNorth on November 9th.
claims.verbatim: announced November 9, 2026
claims.notes: Natalie Spaulding, November 10th. Corroborated by Crypto Briefing (Kaye Quema, published Monday November 9th, 11:45 a.m. EST): 'Governor Mike Dunleavy said Monday'. NO PRIMARY: gov.alaska.gov/newsroom/page/2/ lists only items from July 16th to September 18th and contains no AKDC or InvestNorth release. Page 1 was not fetched this run, and scouts A and F report that it held only proclamations.

claims.claim: Alaska Data Corporation's own website describes it as a subsidiary of AIDEA.
claims.verbatim: AKDC is a subsidiary of AIDEA and is authorized under AS 44.88.178.
claims.notes: The page carries no date other than a 2026 copyright line, so date_of_source is the access date. Also supported by the primary Resolution G26-03, which says the Authority 'has established a subsidiary that is a limited liability company known as Alaska Data Corporation, LLC' (out/2026-11-12/pdf/g26_03.txt lines 54 to 56). CONFLICT RESOLVED: the TechFlow rewrite of Bloomberg calls it 'a company under the state's Economic Development Division'. The primary documents contradict that, so the deck should not use it.

claims.claim: Must Read Alaska reported that Alaska Data Corporation is a wholly owned AIDEA subsidiary meant to put state capital to work alongside private developers.
claims.verbatim: As a wholly owned AIDEA subsidiary, AKDC is intended to put state capital to work alongside private developers
claims.notes: akdc.com names AIDEA as the owner. Crypto Briefing says 'Alaska Data Corporation will operate as an AIDEA subsidiary'. The exact words 'wholly owned' appear only in the Must Read Alaska text.

claims.claim: Alaska Data Corporation says it is authorized under AS 44.88.178.
claims.verbatim: AKDC is a subsidiary of AIDEA and is authorized under AS 44.88.178.
claims.notes: Resolution G26-03 cites the same statute as the authority to create the subsidiary (g26_03.txt lines 40 to 42 and 47 to 48).

claims.claim: Alaska Data Corporation lists Brandon Brefczynski as its President.
claims.verbatim: Brandon Brefczynski President
claims.notes: On the page the name and the title sit on consecutive lines ('Brandon Brefczynski' / 'President'). This text came from the targeted repeat fetch. Must Read Alaska and the Alaska Beacon feed summary also name him AKDC president.

claims.claim: Alaska Data Corporation names Dave Stieren as its Vice President and media contact.
claims.verbatim: Media inquiries go to Vice President Dave Stieren.
claims.notes: The repeat fetch confirmed the leadership lines 'Dave Stieren' / 'Vice President'. The Beacon feed calls him a former conservative talk radio host, but that detail is RSS body text and is not verified here.

claims.claim: Brandon Brefczynski was AIDEA's Deputy Director when he co-signed the staff memo for Resolution G26-03.
claims.verbatim: Brandon Brefczynski, Deputy Director
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority
claims.notes: Verified from local extraction out/2026-11-12/pdf/g26_03.txt, lines 155 to 158. The memo is from Randy Ruaro, Executive Director, and Brefczynski, and is dated January 21, 2026. Background document for this run.

claims.claim: Alaska Data Corporation says its records may be subject to disclosure under the Alaska Public Records Act.
claims.verbatim: Records of Alaska Data Corporation LLC may be subject to public disclosure under the Alaska Public Records Act (AS 40.25).
claims.notes: Keep 'may be'. The page does not say every record is public.

claims.claim: Alaska Data Corporation states its purpose as identifying, developing and accelerating investments in emerging technologies.
claims.verbatim: The purpose of Alaska Data Corporation is to identify, develop, and accelerate investments.
claims.notes: The page lists digital infrastructure, energy tech and digital platforms. According to the fetch response it does not mention data centers by name, only 'energy-efficient digital infrastructure'. Treat that as a reported absence from one fetch, not a claim.

claims.claim: Alaska Data Corporation's website describes the company as a Delaware corporation.
claims.verbatim: Alaska Data Corporation LLC is a Delaware corporation
claims.notes: The page uses 'corporation' for an entity named LLC. The resolution calls it a limited liability company. If the deck mentions this, say 'organized in Delaware' and do not call it a corporation.

claims.claim: InvestNorth was announced as a state-sponsored infrastructure financing platform.
claims.verbatim: a state-sponsored infrastructure financing platform
claims.notes: Must Read Alaska uses the same phrase: 'a state-sponsored infrastructure financing platform called'. investnorth.com returned only its title, so there is no primary text for InvestNorth.

claims.claim: InvestNorth will use tokenization to digitize ownership interests in infrastructure assets.
claims.verbatim: InvestNorth will use tokenization to digitize ownership interests in infrastructure assets.
claims.notes: Must Read Alaska says 'The platform uses tokenization, a process that represents ownership interests in an asset through digital records.'

claims.claim: InvestNorth runs on AssetOS, software from the fintech company Plural.
claims.verbatim: InvestNorth uses AssetOS to coordinate investor commitments
claims.notes: Must Read Alaska says InvestNorth 'operates on the company's AssetOS platform', and the company there is Plural. Crypto Briefing describes Plural as 'a financial technology company serving energy and digital infrastructure developers'.

claims.claim: Plural holds SEC transfer agent registration and FINRA broker-dealer registration.
claims.verbatim: Plural holds SEC transfer agent registration and FINRA broker-dealer registration.
claims.notes: Crypto Briefing adds detail: 'The company holds SEC registration as a transfer agent' and 'its brokerage subsidiary is registered with FINRA as a broker-dealer.' The broker-dealer registration belongs to a subsidiary. Neither SEC nor FINRA records were checked.

claims.claim: Alaska Data Corporation is meant to facilitate distributed data centers in communities throughout the state.
claims.verbatim: facilitate the development of distributed data centers in communities throughout the state.
claims.notes: Crypto Briefing has 'to establish distributed data centers in communities across the state'. Do not use the brief's phrasing 'communities statewide' as a quote, because neither page says it.

claims.claim: Some InvestNorth opportunities could be reserved for Alaska residents.
claims.verbatim: certain opportunities potentially reserved exclusively for Alaska residents
claims.notes: This is conditional, so write 'potentially' or 'could be'. Crypto Briefing has 'investment options specifically reserved for Alaska residents' framed as something the state will explore.

claims.claim: No InvestNorth investment offering was available when the platform was announced.
claims.verbatim: No investment offering is currently available
claims.notes: This was true as of November 10th. Corroborated by the Alaska Beacon/Anchorage Press feed summary (the platform 'listed no offerings yet', paraphrased) and by investnorth.com, which showed only a title when fetched November 13th.

claims.claim: The administration did not announce specific data center projects or construction schedules with the launch.
claims.verbatim: The administration has not announced specific data center projects, construction schedules,
claims.notes: Corroborated by absence. None of Crypto Briefing, the TechFlow/Bloomberg rewrite, akdc.com or investnorth.com names a project. Locations are NOT confirmed as unannounced. The article says only that AKDC will 'identify locations' with developers, so the 'no sites' claim was killed.

claims.claim: The administration did not announce investment amounts or projected job totals with the launch.
claims.value: no dollar amounts or job totals
claims.verbatim: investment amounts or projected job totals as part of this announcement.
claims.notes: This continues the sentence quoted in C18. None of the other fetched launch coverage gives an investor dollar figure or a job count. The $20 million capitalization (C26) is AIDEA money from January and is not an offering size.

claims.claim: The administration did not outline the financial terms for deploying AIDEA capital alongside private developers.
claims.verbatim: Nor has it outlined the financial terms under which AIDEA capital would be deployed alongside private developers.
claims.notes: Corroborated by absence across the other fetched coverage.

claims.claim: Any InvestNorth opportunity would have to be offered through SEC- and FINRA-compliant channels.
claims.verbatim: any investment opportunities would have to be offered through SEC- and FINRA-compliant channels
claims.notes: Crypto Briefing has 'must comply with applicable federal and state securities laws, FINRA rules and regulatory approvals.' Neither source names the securities exemption.

claims.claim: Dunleavy said the state should explore how individual Alaskans can have an ownership stake.
claims.verbatim: let's explore how individual Alaskans can have an ownership stake
claims.notes: The same words appear on Crypto Briefing, a second independent fetch. This is a fragment of a longer sentence, so quote it only as a fragment. The apostrophe was normalized to straight.

claims.claim: Brefczynski said tokenization was an obvious choice to make projects more transparent, accessible and automated.
claims.verbatim: tokenization was an obvious choice to make projects more transparent, accessible, and automated,
claims.notes: This is verbatim only on Must Read Alaska. Crypto Briefing paraphrases it with different words ('a natural fit for making infrastructure projects easier to access, monitor and administer'). If the deck quotes it, use the Must Read Alaska wording exactly and attribute it to the announcement.

claims.claim: Plural CEO Adam Silver called the infrastructure behind AI one of the greatest economic opportunities of our time.
claims.verbatim: The infrastructure behind AI is one of the greatest economic opportunities of our time,
claims.notes: This is promotional language from the vendor, so attribute it to Silver. Crypto Briefing carries the apparent continuation: 'Alaska has recognized that capturing it requires new ways to finance it,'.

claims.claim: AIDEA Resolution G26-03 is titled as authorizing an inquiry by Alaska Data Corporation into blockchain and other financing technologies.
claims.verbatim: AUTHORIZING AN INQUIRY BY ALASKA DATA CORPORATION, LLC INTO THE APPLICATION OF BLOCKCHAIN AND OTHER FINANCING TECHNOLOGIES
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority
claims.notes: Verified from local extraction out/2026-11-12/pdf/g26_03.txt, lines 5 to 8 (line breaks collapsed). The minutes repeat the title in the motion (aidea_minutes_jan21.txt lines 244 to 246). Background document from January.

claims.claim: Resolution G26-03 approves a transfer of $20,000,000 from AIDEA's Revolving Fund to Alaska Data Corporation.
claims.verbatim: The Board of the Authority approves the transfer of $20,000,000 from the Revolving Fund
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority
claims.notes: Verified from local extraction out/2026-11-12/pdf/g26_03.txt, lines 101 to 104 (Section 2). The signed text includes the figure that was inserted by amendment at the meeting (see C36). Corroborated by the Alaska Beacon/Anchorage Press feed summary ('$20 million' for Alaska Data Corp., allocated earlier this year) and the January 21st minutes. As a sanity check, $20 million is twice the $10 million annual operating budget Brefczynski cited (C40).

claims.claim: Resolution G26-03 directs Alaska Data Corporation to record the transfer as equity and working capital.
claims.verbatim: directs that ADC LLC record that contribution as equity, and working capital.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority
claims.notes: Verified from local extraction out/2026-11-12/pdf/g26_03.txt, lines 103 to 104.

claims.claim: Under Section 7 of G26-03, the platform may be developed only after the inquiry finds it feasible and in the public interest and AIDEA's Chief Financial Officer approves.
claims.verbatim: once they have completed the Inquiry, determined it to be feasible and in the public interest; and received approval to proceed from the Authority's Chief Financial Officer
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority
claims.notes: Verified from local extraction out/2026-11-12/pdf/g26_03.txt, lines 129 to 133. The source has a curly apostrophe, normalized here. The text continues 'or the designee of the Chief Financial Officer'. Nothing fetched this run shows whether the feasibility finding or the CFO approval has happened. Do not assert either way.

claims.claim: The AIDEA staff memo for G26-03 left the transfer amount blank in its request section.
claims.verbatim: The resolution also authorizes the transfer of $__________from the Revolving Fund
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority
claims.notes: Verified from local extraction out/2026-11-12/pdf/g26_03.txt, line 178. The same memo states the figure later (C30), so the memo is internally inconsistent. Do not call the memo wholly blank.

claims.claim: The same staff memo later states a capitalization of $20,000,000 in equity and working capital.
claims.verbatim: the capitalization of ADC LLC with $ 20,000,000 in equity and working capital
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority
claims.notes: Verified from local extraction out/2026-11-12/pdf/g26_03.txt, lines 244 to 245. The minutes agree that the $20 million request was 'included in the memorandum' (aidea_minutes_jan21.txt lines 211 to 213).

claims.claim: The text of Resolution G26-03 and its staff memo never uses the words data center.
claims.verbatim: evaluating the feasibility of establishing a tokenization and digital asset blockchain platform
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority
claims.notes: Checked absence. I read the full local extraction out/2026-11-12/pdf/g26_03.txt, lines 1 to 259, and found no 'data center', which agrees with the showrunner's grep (0 hits). The verbatim quote is the Section 1 statement of what the inquiry evaluates (lines 97 to 98). OCR text can drop words, so phrase this as 'the resolution text does not mention data centers'. Data centers do come up at the meeting itself (C46, C47).

claims.claim: Resolution G26-03 calls Alaska Data Corporation AIDEA's technological advances development subsidiary.
claims.verbatim: which is the Authority's technological advances development subsidiary
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority
claims.notes: Verified from local extraction out/2026-11-12/pdf/g26_03.txt, lines 55 to 56. The apostrophe was normalized.

claims.claim: Brandon Brefczynski presented Resolution G26-03 to the AIDEA board on January 21st.
claims.verbatim: Acting Chair Kendig requested Brandon Brefczynski, Deputy Director, to present Resolution G26-03.
claims.notes: Verified from local extraction out/2026-11-12/pdf/aidea_minutes_jan21.txt, lines 168 to 170. The meeting was January 21, 2026, by teleconference (lines 6 to 8). The minutes were signed later, and 2026-03-18 comes from the filename. They are a staff summary, not a transcript.

claims.claim: Brefczynski told the board G26-03 would establish an AIDEA subsidiary named Alaska Data Corporation focused on technology investments.
claims.verbatim: will establish an AIDEA subsidiary named Alaska Data Corporation, LLC, which will focus on investments in the technology sector, innovation, and emerging opportunities
claims.notes: Verified from local extraction aidea_minutes_jan21.txt, lines 170 to 172. These are the minutes' paraphrase of his remarks, so do not put them in quotation marks as his own words.

claims.claim: According to the minutes, the capitalization amount was left blank in the resolution put before the board.
claims.verbatim: the capitalization amount for the subsidiary was left blank in the resolution
claims.notes: Verified from local extraction aidea_minutes_jan21.txt, lines 210 to 214. Brefczynski said the board would need to amend the resolution to capitalize the subsidiary that day.

claims.claim: Board member Albert Fogle amended his motion to insert the $20 million capitalization recommended by staff.
claims.verbatim: Mr. Fogle amended his motion to insert the capitalization number of $20 million, as recommended by staff.
claims.notes: Verified from local extraction aidea_minutes_jan21.txt, lines 257 to 260. Fogle's first name is from the roll call at lines 14 to 16.

claims.claim: G26-03 passed unanimously on a roll call with Commissioner Julie Sande absent.
claims.verbatim: to insert the capitalization number of $20 million, passed unanimously, with Commissioner Sande absent.
claims.notes: Verified from local extraction aidea_minutes_jan21.txt, lines 261 to 263 ('A roll call was taken'). Sande appears as present at the opening roll call (line 14), so she was absent for this vote, not for the whole meeting. The minutes record no individual tally, so the number of yes votes is not stated.

claims.claim: Board member Andrew Guy said the requested capitalization seemed high and asked to see a budget for the funds.
claims.verbatim: the requested capitalization amount seems high. He stated that he would be more comfortable in seeing a budget for the use of the funds.
claims.notes: Verified from local extraction aidea_minutes_jan21.txt, lines 215 to 217. This is a minutes paraphrase, so write 'according to the minutes'. It was Guy's first meeting (line 339). He then voted in the unanimous yes.

claims.claim: Brefczynski told the board AIDEA has a $1.7 billion balance sheet.
claims.verbatim: AIDEA has a $1.7 billion balance sheet with an annual operating budget of $10 million a year.
claims.notes: Verified from local extraction aidea_minutes_jan21.txt, lines 224 to 225. The figure is attributed to Brefczynski in the minutes and was not audited here. Write 'Brefczynski told the board'. As a sanity check, $20 million is about 1.2 percent of $1.7 billion.

claims.claim: Brefczynski told the board AIDEA's annual operating budget is $10 million.
claims.verbatim: AIDEA has a $1.7 billion balance sheet with an annual operating budget of $10 million a year.
claims.notes: Verified from local extraction aidea_minutes_jan21.txt, lines 224 to 225. Attribute to Brefczynski. The $20 million capitalization equals two years of that stated operating budget.

claims.claim: Brefczynski described the $20 million as a multi-year capitalization of the subsidiary.
claims.verbatim: the request amount reflects a multi-year capitalization of the subsidiary
claims.notes: Verified from local extraction aidea_minutes_jan21.txt, lines 226 to 227. The extraction has extra spaces around 'multi-year capitalization', collapsed here.

claims.claim: Brefczynski said the subsidiary was not intended to return to the board for more capitalization.
claims.verbatim: without the intent of returning to the Board for future capitalization
claims.notes: Verified from local extraction aidea_minutes_jan21.txt, lines 228 to 229. Lines 218 to 219 say the same thing: 'it is not the intent that the subsidiary ADC, LLC would request additional funding from AIDEA.' This was a stated intent, not a binding limit.

claims.claim: The $20 million was described as covering operations and due diligence costs for potential investments.
claims.verbatim: million for the capitalization of ADC , LLC includes the operation and due diligence costs for potential investments.
claims.notes: Verified from local extraction aidea_minutes_jan21.txt, lines 222 to 224. The full sentence begins 'The requested $20'. The verbatim keeps the extraction's stray space before the comma.

claims.claim: Brefczynski told the board the platform would show accredited and non-accredited retail investors the offerings each is eligible for.
claims.verbatim: if an offer is specifically available to accredited investors, then they could be able to access that offering. Likewise, if offerings are investible by citizens and retail investors who are not accredited, they will be able to see those offerings.
claims.notes: Verified from local extraction aidea_minutes_jan21.txt, lines 186 to 191. Minutes paraphrase. He described a plan, not a live feature.

claims.claim: Adam Silver of Plural presented on tokenization to the AIDEA board two meetings before the January 21st vote.
claims.verbatim: two Board meetings ago, Adam Silver of Plural gave a presentation on tokenization.
claims.notes: Verified from local extraction aidea_minutes_jan21.txt, lines 183 to 184. The minutes add that Silver was available that day to answer questions. The date of the earlier meeting is not stated. The previous minutes approved were from December 10, 2025, but the earlier presentation date was not verified.

claims.claim: At the January meeting Brefczynski linked the platform to a shift toward electron-based assets, data centers and AI.
claims.verbatim: the world moves toward electron-based assets, data centers, AI, and others.
claims.notes: Verified from local extraction aidea_minutes_jan21.txt, lines 203 to 208. This minutes paraphrase is the only place data centers come up in the G26-03 discussion apart from the Cordova loan (C47). Contrast with C31, the resolution text.

claims.claim: Brefczynski said the AIDEA board had approved a loan for a small data center deployment in Cordova, with closing nearly complete.
claims.verbatim: the AIDEA Board approved AIDEA to issue a loan for a small data center deployment in Cordova. AIDEA is nearing completion of the closing
claims.notes: Verified from local extraction aidea_minutes_jan21.txt, lines 220 to 222. He said it was approved 'last year', meaning 2025. The loan amount and borrower are not stated, and whether it has since closed was not checked.

claims.claim: Brefczynski told the board that broadening the range of investors would require work with the SEC and the Department of Law.
claims.verbatim: work with the federal government , the SEC, and the Department of Law would occur if AIDEA wanted to broaden the scope and range of potential investors
claims.notes: Verified from local extraction aidea_minutes_jan21.txt, lines 181 to 182. Minutes paraphrase.

claims.claim: In public comment, Fairbanks resident John Gaedeke called it alarming that the day's resolutions added less oversight and more money.
claims.verbatim: it is alarming that the resolutions today effectively add less oversight and more money
claims.notes: Verified from local extraction aidea_minutes_jan21.txt, lines 34 to 56. He spoke about the day's resolutions generally, naming 'getting into blockchain' and the $3 million asset management budget (G26-01), not G26-03 alone. Minutes paraphrase, a one-sided opinion, so attribute it to him.

claims.claim: The next governor takes office at noon on December 7th, the first Monday in December after the election.
claims.verbatim: The term of office of the governor is four years, beginning at noon on the first Monday in December following his election
claims.source_outlet: Constitution of the State of Alaska, Article III, Section 4 (text via Wikisource)
claims.notes: Re-sourced 2026-11-13 at scoring: the earlier Alaska Public Media URL (November 3rd, 'The winner is set to take office at noon Dec. 7.') carries a slug naming a candidate as leading, against the deck's never-imply-the-winner guard. The first Monday in December 2026 is December 7th (computed). ltgov.alaska.gov returned 503 and akleg.gov 403 at fetch time. Alaska Public Media remains corroboration in the evidence record only.

claims.claim: Ranked choice tabulation is scheduled for November 18th.
claims.verbatim: In some races, the winner will be determined in ranked choice tabulation, which is scheduled to take place Nov. 18.
claims.notes: Mari Kanagy. Alaska Public Media's November 3rd story also gives the November 18th tally date. The Division of Elections primary was not fetched.

claims.claim: Final certification of the election results is scheduled for November 25th.
claims.verbatim: Final certification of results is scheduled for Nov. 25.
claims.notes: Corroborated by the TechFlow/Bloomberg rewrite ('Alaska plans to complete vote counting on November 25'). The Alaska Public Media November 3rd article does not mention certification.

claims.claim: On November 12th the Alaska Beacon republished an Anchorage Press story by Max Graham headlined about AIDEA going on a spending spree before the new governor arrives.
claims.verbatim: Weeks before Alaska gets a new governor, its economic development arm goes on a spending spree
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon (RSS feed, story by Max Graham, Anchorage Press)
claims.notes: Feed pubDate Thu, 12 Nov 2026 20:05:08 +0000, dc:creator 'Max Graham, Anchorage Press'. The article page itself returns 403. The Anchorage Press homepage lists the original as November 11th, 9:23 AM AKST. Per the brief, the RSS is used for this headline-level claim only.

claims.claim: The Anchorage Press reported that AIDEA has directed more than $200 million to a spate of projects over the past few months.
claims.verbatim: An embattled state corporation has directed more than $200 million to a spate of projects over the past few months.
claims.notes: This is the story's dek as shown on the Anchorage Press homepage (story by Max Graham, November 11th). It is a total the newspaper compiled and was not rebuilt from primary records here, so write 'according to the Anchorage Press'. The Beacon feed summary agrees: more than $200 million announced since August. The itemized breakdown is RSS body text and was killed.

stories_surviving: Alaska Data Corporation and InvestNorth, the November 9th tokenized data center finance launch, and the January AIDEA resolution behind it

killed.claim: A governor's office press release announced AKDC and InvestNorth on November 9th.
killed.why: No primary found. gov.alaska.gov/newsroom/page/2/ shows items from July 16th to September 18th only. The announcement rests on Must Read Alaska and Crypto Briefing (C01).

killed.claim: InvestNorth's website describes the platform, its sponsor or its offerings.
killed.why: investnorth.com returned only the title 'InvestNorth' with no other text.

killed.claim: No data center sites or locations were announced.
killed.why: Must Read Alaska does not say so. It says only that AKDC will 'identify locations' with developers. C18 and C19 cover what the article does say was not announced.

killed.claim: Alaska Data is a company under the state's Economic Development Division.
killed.why: This is from the TechFlow retranslation of Bloomberg. akdc.com, Resolution G26-03 and the January 21st minutes all make it an AIDEA subsidiary.

killed.claim: Quotes from Brefczynski ('It represents a forward step...'), Dunleavy ('This model will take root...') and Silver ('You can be a resident voicing concerns...') via TechFlow.
killed.why: TechFlow's text is 'Compiled by Chopper, Foresight News', a retranslation of a Bloomberg story. The wording isn't the speakers' verbatim words, the Bloomberg original wasn't fetched (403 per scouts), and a named-person quote must be verbatim.

killed.claim: Bloomberg reported the state is promoting data center projects while simultaneously issuing related investment products, with liquidity and investor protection unresolved.
killed.why: Only source is a retranslated secondary (TechFlow). There is no primary and no second independent source, so the framing can't be attributed to Bloomberg's own words.

killed.claim: This year's Permanent Fund Dividend is $1,200.
killed.why: Only source is the TechFlow retranslation of Bloomberg. It was not checked against the PFD Division and has no second source.

killed.claim: The once-proposed North Slope data center was 3 gigawatts, equal to 2.4 million households.
killed.why: Single retranslated secondary (TechFlow). The household equivalence is Bloomberg's yardstick and was not verified.

killed.claim: 44 ballot measures restricting data center development had been approved nationally.
killed.why: Crypto Briefing attributes it to the Data Centers on the Ballot tracker, which wasn't fetched. Single secondary, and it's from outside Alaska.

killed.claim: Kreiss-Tomkins said he would 'completely reassess' AIDEA.
killed.why: This appears only in the Beacon RSS body. The article page returns 403, and the brief limits the RSS to headline-level claims. The direct quote couldn't be verified on a full article page.

killed.claim: Kreiss-Tomkins has proposed pausing data center approvals.
killed.why: No source fetched this run supports it. The Alaska Public Media November 3rd article makes no mention of data centers, a pause or AIDEA.

killed.claim: Election-night first-choice shares of 49, 29, 14 and 7 percent for Kreiss-Tomkins, Wilson, Bronson and Taylor.
killed.why: These are superseded figures. Alaska Public Media's November 12th headline says JKT has topped 50%. The brief also says not to assert a winner while the count is uncertified.

killed.claim: AIDEA's itemized commitments: $25 million NuCube, up to $75 million broadband subsidiary, up to $10 million GeoAlaska, about $86 million Ambler Road, more than $50 million shipyards, $20 million Alaska Data Corp.
killed.why: These come from the Beacon RSS description and body, which the brief limits to headline-level use. The $20 million figure survives on primary documents instead (C26, C36).

killed.claim: Alaska Data Corporation's website describes it as a data center developer.
killed.why: Per the fetch response, akdc.com doesn't mention data centers by name, only 'energy-efficient digital infrastructure'.

killed.claim: Story 2: Enstar can buy about 1.2 Bcf under an RCA-approved exchange with MEA and Hilcorp, must return it to MEA by March 2028, targets 6 to 7 Bcf versus about 5 Bcf projected, serves about 150,000 members, MEA has 60,000 members, and MEA predicts about $2 million savings from 2027 to 2029.
killed.why: Every figure appears verbatim on the Alaska Public Media page (Ava White, November 6th). John Sims also said 'We don't like to be just in time when we're planning for gas supply, but this is just in time.' But this is one secondary source with no primary. The RCA order was not reached, rca.alaska.gov refuses bots, and the attempts at enstarnaturalgas.com/newsroom/ and mea.coop/news/ both returned 404. Killed under the single-source rule.

killed.claim: Story 3: Waymo is cold-weather testing its sixth-generation Waymo Driver around Fairbanks, with manual data collection, specialist-supervised autonomous driving and limited structured testing, and has charged at GVEA's parking lot.
killed.why: This is verbatim on Alaska's News Source (Alex Bengel, dated November 10th although the URL says 11/11), which quotes Waymo's Chris Bonelli and GVEA's Ashley Bradish. But it is a single secondary source with no Waymo primary, and the second-source attempt at newsminer.com returned 429. Killed under the single-source rule.
